newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays in range, direction uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays in range, direction uncertain.

text.p: The ringgit stayed rangebound in late afternoon Asian trading amid thin volumes and dealers said future direction was uncertain.
They said lack of volumes and a mild lull in dollar/majors had also kept the ringgit relatively inactive.
"The market has moved in a 40-point range for the whole day. Technically it is in a very strong (dollar) support range," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
But a generally low level of activity in the majors ahead of Japanese Sakakibara's appearance on television, had further reduced trading in the exotics, they said.
Some dealers said ringgit may break out of the current range and head back towards 2.53 level. But others said fresh funds are expected to flow into the ringgit soon.
Research firm I.D.E.A. in Singapore said close to $500 million in funds raised by Malaysian companies abroad may head back into the country.
"This... would help cancel out much of the traditional year-end rise in dollar-demand," the research firm said.
At 0800 GMT, ringgit was at 2.5209/16 a dollar against 2.5214/21 at the local close on Wednesday.
